sections.h2: How fast can I sell a house in Vancouver, WA?
sections.html:
Speed depends on the buyer's funds, the title work and one county step that every Clark County deed has to pass. A buyer paying cash takes the lender out of the timeline, which is why people facing a move, an inherited house or a repair bill often ask for cash offers. A regular listing adds showings, an appraisal and a loan approval.

Vancouver is the Clark County seat, on the north bank of the Columbia River directly across from Portland. About 199,698 people live here, 4.6 percent more than in 2020. That growth brings plenty of buyers and investors to the same streets you live on, so collecting more than one offer is realistic.

With 50.8 percent of homes lived in by their owners, about half of Vancouver housing is rented. A house that needs work can appeal to a landlord or investor as much as to a buyer who plans to move in.

West Vancouver holds downtown and most of the older housing. East Vancouver grew after the 1997 annexation, which added 11,258 acres and 58,171 residents, and NE Andresen Road is the usual dividing line.

Several well-known neighborhoods began as wartime housing. When the Kaiser shipyard drew tens of thousands of workers in the 1940s, the Vancouver Housing Authority was created along with six developments: Fruit Valley, Fourth Plain Village, Bagley Downs, Ogden Meadows, Burton Homes and McLoughlin Heights. In those areas a buyer's inspector will look hard at age-related items.

  • Original wiring and panels
  • Galvanized or older supply plumbing
  • Foundations, crawl spaces and drainage
  • Roofs and insulation

Inspectors also focus on the roof, gutters and crawl space because the area gets about 42 inches of rain a year, mostly from fall through spring. Check those spots before you set a price.

More than a third of the Vancouver urban area lives in unincorporated pockets such as Hazel Dell, Felida, Orchards and Salmon Creek. Find out whether your address is inside city limits, since the permit and rental rules below apply only there.

Vancouver Public Schools covers most of west Vancouver, and Evergreen Public Schools covers most of the east side. Small portions of the city fall in the Camas and Battle Ground districts, so check the district against your street address before you describe it to a buyer.

Interstates 5 and 205 both cross the Columbia into Portland, SR 14 runs east from downtown, and SR 500 links I-5 to I-205. Rush-hour traffic is heavy on the Interstate Bridge and the Glenn Jackson Bridge, and C-Tran runs local and express buses. Homes near the freeways often appeal to commuters who value a shorter trip.

sections.h2: Do I need a permit before selling a Vancouver house?
sections.html:
Only if you plan to do the work yourself before closing. The city requires a residential building permit to construct, alter, add to, repair or demolish residential buildings. Projects that need one include:

  • Additions and remodels
  • Adding a garage, carport, deck or patio cover
  • Adding or removing walls
  • Converting a basement, attic or garage into living space
  • Changing the footprint of a structure

Small stand-alone electrical, mechanical or plumbing jobs fall under a trade permit instead, and tree removal needs a city permit. If you suspect past work was done without a permit, the city offers a field evaluation permit, where inspectors decide which permits and corrections are needed. The Permit Center answers questions at 360-487-7833.

The city's updated zoning code allows more middle housing, up to six units on one lot. A buyer with development plans may value a lot differently than someone who just wants to move in.

Landlords selling inside city limits should know about two programs. Since January 1, 2026, owners of residential rentals in Vancouver register each unit every year for $30 per unit. Health and safety inspections are planned to begin in mid 2027.

When a registered rental sells, the registration moves to the new owner within 60 days of the property transfer, with no extra fee. If you stop renting, you can deregister the property. Questions go to rentalregistration@cityofvancouver.us or 360-487-7928.

Short-term rentals need a separate permit. Vancouver defines one as a rental of fewer than 30 consecutive nights. The permit calls for a Washington business license with the city endorsement, at least $1 million in liability insurance and a notice mailed to abutting neighbors. Permits are capped at 870, about 1 percent of the housing stock. A permit does not override a lease or homeowners association rules, so a buyer who plans to use the house this way should confirm status on the city's short-term rental page.

sections.h2: Deed and excise tax in Clark County
sections.html:
Every Clark County sale goes to the Treasurer first and the Auditor second. The Treasurer collects the real estate excise tax, and RCW 82.45.090 bars the Auditor from taking a deed for recording until the tax is paid or the Treasurer marks it not due.

The tax is due 30 days from the date of sale, and a $5 processing fee is added. The state part is graduated by sale price:

  • 1.10 percent on a price up to $525,000
  • 1.28 percent from $525,000.01 to $1,525,000
  • 2.75 percent from $1,525,000.01 to $3,025,000
  • 3.00 percent above $3,025,000

A local rate is added on top, so ask the Treasurer or your closing agent for the total on your price. In person, the Treasurer is at 1300 Franklin Street, 2nd Floor, Monday to Thursday from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. After payment, the Auditor's Recording Department at the same address records the deed, and you can reach it at 564-397-2208.

RCW 64.06.020 sets out the disclosure form for improved residential property. The seller hands it over no later than five business days after a written purchase contract is accepted by both sides, unless the parties pick another schedule. The buyer then has a three-business-day window to rescind.

List any known unpermitted work on the form. An as-is sale does not remove this duty, though it does mean you are not agreeing to make repairs.

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal or loan approval, so the house does not have to meet a lender's condition standards. You still deal with the same Clark County steps: the disclosure form, the excise tax at the Treasurer, and recording at the Auditor. A title or escrow company normally carries the paperwork through both offices for you.

Before accepting any offer, compare what you would net after commission, repairs and carrying costs, ask who pays the excise tax, and get the closing date in writing. If the house is a rental, ask how the buyer will handle the tenant and the registration transfer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Vancouver, WA house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes, as-is sales are common. The state's disclosure form under RCW 64.06.020 still applies to improved residential property, and unpermitted work you know of belongs on it.

faqs.q: Who records the deed when a Vancouver house sells?
faqs.a: The Clark County Auditor's Recording Department, but only after the Treasurer handles the excise tax affidavit. Both offices are at 1300 Franklin Street, and title or escrow companies normally submit the paperwork for you.

faqs.q: What happens to my Vancouver rental registration when I sell?
faqs.a: It moves to the new owner within 60 days of the property transfer, with no additional fee. If the buyer will live in the home, the registration can be ended through deregistration.

faqs.q: Does Vancouver cap short-term rental permits?
faqs.a: Yes. Permits are limited to 870, about 1 percent of the housing stock. A buyer who wants to run the house as a short-term rental should check permit availability with the Permit Center before paying extra for that use.

faqs.q: Which school district is my Vancouver house in?
faqs.a: Most of west Vancouver is in Vancouver Public Schools and most of east Vancouver is in Evergreen Public Schools. Small portions are in the Camas and Battle Ground districts, so check the address with the district.
